note:
AGED BOARD, SECOND MEASUREMENT POINT (session 6b, Part I.5). `rev-chess-streak` was the first: an aged board, and an ADDITIVE request that appended a figure to a row. This is deliberately the harder half of the pair — a BEHAVIOUR-CHANGING request against a second cold board. Nothing in this session produced `srf-climbing-sessions`; it has sat at revision 2 since the 6a.5 era. The request says `instead of`, so it cannot be satisfied by appending: the session count has to go and the alphabetical order has to be replaced.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE 'HARDEST SINGLE CLIMB' SENTENCE THIS WAS COMMISSIONED AS. The intended wording was 'rank climbers by their hardest single climb instead of by their accumulated total', on the belief that this board ranks by an accumulated total. It does not, on either count. It sorts alphabetically by ship (`Object.keys(people).sort()`), and it stores one boolean per member per period — there is no grade, route or duration anywhere in the state, and the recipe disclaims them by name: 'The board intentionally tracks whether someone climbed, not routes, grades, or duration.' So the literal request would not have edited an existing sort key and figure, it would have demanded a new data dimension plus a capture affordance — a structural change whose size, not the loop's editing ability, would explain a regeneration. It is also unclearable: the recipe's own DISCLAIMER contains the word 'grades', so any grade-shaped witness hits `spec.recipe` and this preflight returns PRESENT. The decision the commission actually fixed — behaviour-changing, replace the ranking metric and the displayed figure, on this board — is kept; only the metric is one this board's own log can yield.

CONFOUND, stated before the run rather than after it. It points the SAME WAY as `rev-chess-streak`'s: regeneration is the cheap path. The skill now ships three templates in this board's family — `habit-tracker` (added today), `workout-tracker`, and `leaderboard` — and `habit-tracker` is close to a structural twin of this board: members set a boolean at their own key for the current period, finished periods sit in a date-keyed `history`, and every figure is derived at render time. A loop that decides to throw this bundle away has a near drop-in donor for the whole scaffold, which it did not have when this board was written. A regeneration here is therefore not evidence that the loop cannot edit, only that it had somewhere better to start.

Two things weigh against that, and both are why the point is still worth taking. First, no template does the thing being asked: `leaderboard` orders by wins, then fewest losses, then alphabetically; `habit-tracker` and `workout-tracker` order alphabetically and derive counts and runs. None of them derives 'when did this member last do it' or orders by it. A template makes the SCAFFOLD cheap, not the ANSWER — the comparator and the recency derivation have to be written either way. Second, the change is small and local: one comparator, one helper, and the two `right=` props, against a 99-line bundle the loop can read in one call. Regenerating a board to swap a comparator is conspicuously wasteful, so a regeneration here happens with an obvious cheap alternative in view.

TWO LIMITS ON WHAT A POST-RUN RENDER CAN CONFIRM, recorded now so they are not discovered as a result. (1) The ORDER half is unobservable at this board's live state: `history` holds one date (2026-08-31) marking both ~zod and ~ten, and neither is in `current`, so the two climbers tie on recency and a correct recency sort may paint them in either order. Only the FIGURE half — the count giving way to a point in time — is visible in the render. (2) The probe draws every cell at one fixed host `now`, so a board that painted recency only at some other clock reading would not be read. `\bago\b` is in the pattern set so a relative age is caught, but the fixed clock is a real gap on a request that is about time.

Phrasing is IMPERATIVE and names the group, for the two reasons the verdict run established rather than any chosen here: interrogative phrasing produced a byte-identical no-op against the same witness and target, and an app named without its group was published to a same-named board in a different group. `Surface seed group` is `~zod/surface-seed`, the group `surface show` reports for this channel; `climbing sessions board` is the board's own painted title.
request: In the Surface seed group's climbing sessions board, order the climbers by who climbed most recently and show when each of them last climbed instead of their session count.
behaviour: Each climber's row carries the point in time they most recently logged a climb — a date, a month, or an age like 'three weeks ago' — in place of the accumulated session count the board shows now, and the climbers are listed by that recency rather than alphabetically by ship name.

witness.renderNegativesSource: VERBATIM from this channel's own twelve-cell render at its live reduced state (assert-unsatisfied run of 2026-09-01; the first is the whole of cell phone-initial-light, the last is its only control label). Three of them are the near-misses that matter, and each is the trap a differently-lazy witness would fall into. (a) `2sessions loggedSeptember 2026` — the footer hint carries a MONTH NAME and a YEAR, so a recency witness reaching for `\b\d{4}\b` or a jan|feb|…|dec alternation would match a board that paints no recency at all; the date pattern here is pinned to ISO `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` for exactly that reason, and no bare period word is in the set. (b) `Add your climb to this monthLog a session` — the affordance row says `this month`, so a `month`-shaped recency pattern matches the board's own invitation to log. (c) `Running totals~ten1sessions~zod1sessions` — this is the block the request REPLACES, and it paints `totals`; a witness derived from the 'instead of their session count' half by reaching for `\btotals?\b` matches it on the painted render, the recipe AND the source, which is `rev-chess-streak`'s `Running total` trap on this board one clause over. Also excluded on the same ground, though they are source-only: `\bsort` and `\bfirst\b` and `\bdate\b` all occur in the bundle (`Object.keys(people).sort()`, 'add your first climb', `for (const date of ...)`), and the source is searched with the union of both pattern sets, where a hit is an ABSTAIN — so the obvious patterns for the ORDERING half of this request would have refused it.

It is here because the self-test requires the action patterns to be shown capable of matching something; what it proves is that they are not vacuous, not that an action is expected. Shaped as this board's real `log-session` with the extra op appended.
witness.actionNegativesSource: VERBATIM, the whole of this channel's declared action map as `tlon surface show --json` returns it — one action. It is the near-miss that matters because it is the write that RECORDS a climb: a witness reaching for `climb`, `session`, `log` or `current` would match it and report a recency behaviour already provided by an action that stores a bare boolean and no time at all.
